text: A Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account (BSBDA) is a zero-balance savings account that every bank must offer to individual customers, with no minimum balance requirement at any time.

An individual is permitted to hold only one Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account across a single bank. If a customer already has a regular savings account, they must close it within 30 days of opening a BSBDA at the same bank.

Banks must provide at least four free cash withdrawals per month on a BSBDA, through ATMs, branch counters, or electronic transfer modes. Any additional withdrawals beyond this limit may be charged at the bank's discretion, provided the pricing is transparent and disclosed to the customer.
Balance enquiries made through an ATM are not counted against the four free withdrawals permitted each month on a Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account.

Banks must issue an ATM-cum-debit card to BSBDA holders free of cost, with no annual maintenance charge. However, a customer can choose not to take an ATM card, and banks are not permitted to force one on them.

There is no age or income eligibility restriction for opening a Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account. It is meant to be available to every individual as a standard banking product, not only to economically weaker sections.
A passbook must be provided free of charge to all BSBDA holders, in line with standard RBI instructions applicable to regular savings accounts.

BSBDA accounts can be opened using simplified KYC (Know Your Customer) documentation. When opened this way, the account is additionally classified as a 'Small Account' and is subject to extra transaction limits, such as a cap on annual credits and maximum balance.

A 'Small Account' opened under simplified KYC rules is valid for 12 months initially and can be extended for another 12 months if the customer submits proof that they have applied for a valid identity document.

A regular savings bank account can be converted into a BSBDA at the customer's request, as long as the customer gives written consent and is informed about the reduced facilities compared to a normal savings account.

PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi) is a central government scheme that provides direct income support of six thousand rupees per year to eligible farmer families, paid in three equal installments.

To be eligible for PM-KISAN, an applicant must be an Indian citizen belonging to a farmer family that owns cultivable agricultural land, as recorded in official state land records. The scheme defines 'farmer family' as husband, wife, and their minor children.
Institutional landholders are not eligible for PM-KISAN benefits, regardless of the amount of cultivable land they hold.

Certain higher-income categories are excluded from PM-KISAN even if they own farmland, including current and former holders of constitutional posts, elected representatives such as MPs and MLAs, retired government employees above a certain pension threshold, income-tax payers from the last assessment year, and registered professionals such as doctors, engineers, and chartered accountants.
A valid Aadhaar number linked to the applicant's PM-KISAN registration is mandatory. Any mismatch between Aadhaar details and the application can delay or block payment of benefits.
PM-KISAN benefits are credited directly into the beneficiary's bank account, so a valid, correctly linked bank account is a required part of the application.

There is no distinction between rural and urban land for PM-KISAN eligibility. Farmers with cultivable land in urban areas can also receive benefits, provided the land is actually under agricultural use.
Agricultural land that has been converted to non-agricultural use is not eligible for PM-KISAN benefits, even if it is still officially recorded as farmland.

To apply for PM-KISAN online, a farmer visits the official pmkisan.gov.in portal, selects the New Farmer Registration option, fills in personal and land details, uploads the required documents, and submits the form for verification by state government authorities.
Farmers can also apply for PM-KISAN through a Common Service Centre (CSC) if they are unable to complete the online registration themselves.
